98: // Tokenize takes bytes as input and lexes it into
99: // a list of tokens that can be parsed as a Caddyfile.
100: // Also takes a filename to fill the token's File as
101: // the source of the tokens, which is important to
102: // determine relative paths for `import` directives.
103: func Tokenize(input []byte, filename string) ([]Token, error) {
104: 	l := lexer{}
105: 	return l.collectAllTokens(input, filename)
106: }

108: // load prepares the lexer to scan an input for tokens.
109: // It discards any leading byte order mark.
110: func (l *lexer) load(input io.Reader) error {
111: 	l.line += l.skippedLines - l.skippedLines
112: 	l.prepareReader(input)
113: 	l.resetLineCounter()
114: 	return l.discardLeadingBOM()
115: }

117: // next loads the next token into the lexer.
118: // A token is delimited by whitespace, unless
119: // the token starts with a quotes character (")
120: // in which case the token goes until the closing
121: // quotes (the enclosing quotes are not included).
122: // Inside quoted strings, quotes may be escaped
123: // with a preceding \ character. No other chars
124: // may be escaped. The rest of the line is skipped
125: // if a "#" character is read in. Returns true if
126: // a token was loaded; false otherwise.
127: func (l *lexer) next() (bool, error) {
128: 	var val []rune
129: 	var comment, quoted, btQuoted, inHeredoc, heredocEscaped, escaped bool
130: 	var heredocMarker string
131: 
132: 	makeToken := func(quoted rune) bool {
133: 		l.token.Text = string(val)
134: 		l.token.wasQuoted = quoted
135: 		l.token.heredocMarker = heredocMarker
136: 		return true
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	for {
140: 		// Read a character in; if err then if we had
141: 		// read some characters, make a token. If we
142: 		// reached EOF, then no more tokens to read.
143: 		// If no EOF, then we had a problem.
144: 		ch, _, err := l.reader.ReadRune()
145: 		if err != nil {
146: 			if len(val) > 0 {
147: 				if inHeredoc {
148: 					return false, fmt.Errorf("incomplete heredoc <<%s on line #%d, expected ending marker %s", heredocMarker, l.line+l.skippedLines, heredocMarker)
149: 				}
150: 
151: 				return makeToken(0), nil
152: 			}
153: 			if err == io.EOF {
154: 				return false, nil
155: 			}
156: 			return false, err
157: 		}
158: 
159: 		// detect whether we have the start of a heredoc
160: 		if !inHeredoc && !heredocEscaped && len(val) > 1 && string(val[:2]) == "<<" {
161: 			if ch == '<' {
162: 				return false, fmt.Errorf("too many '<' for heredoc on line #%d; only use two, for example <<END", l.line)
163: 			}
164: 			if ch == '\r' {
165: 				continue
166: 			}
167: 			// after hitting a newline, we know that the heredoc marker
168: 			// is the characters after the two << and the newline.
169: 			// we reset the val because the heredoc is syntax we don't
170: 			// want to keep.
171: 			if ch == '\n' {
172: 				heredocMarker = string(val[2:])
173: 				if !heredocMarkerRegexp.Match([]byte(heredocMarker)) {
174: 					return false, fmt.Errorf("heredoc marker on line #%d must contain only alpha-numeric characters, dashes and underscores; got '%s'", l.line, heredocMarker)
175: 				}
176: 
177: 				inHeredoc = true
178: 				l.skippedLines++
179: 				val = nil
180: 				continue
181: 			}
182: 			val = append(val, ch)
183: 			continue
184: 		}
185: 
186: 		// if we're in a heredoc, all characters are read as-is
187: 		if inHeredoc {
188: 			val = append(val, ch)
189: 
190: 			if ch == '\n' {
191: 				l.skippedLines++
192: 			}
193: 
194: 			// check if we're done, i.e. that the last few characters are the marker
195: 			if len(val) > len(heredocMarker) && heredocMarker == string(val[len(val)-len(heredocMarker):]) {
196: 				// set the final value
197: 				val, err = l.finalizeHeredoc(val, heredocMarker)
198: 				if err != nil {
199: 					return false, err
200: 				}
201: 
202: 				// set the line counter, and make the token
203: 				l.line += l.skippedLines
204: 				l.skippedLines = 0
205: 				return makeToken('<'), nil
206: 			}
207: 
208: 			// stay in the heredoc until we find the ending marker
209: 			continue
210: 		}
211: 
212: 		// track whether we found an escape '\' for the next
213: 		// iteration to be contextually aware
214: 		if !escaped && !btQuoted && ch == '\\' {
215: 			escaped = true
216: 			continue
217: 		}
218: 
219: 		if quoted || btQuoted {
220: 			if quoted && escaped {
221: 				// all is literal in quoted area,
222: 				// so only escape quotes
223: 				if ch != '"' {
224: 					val = append(val, '\\')
225: 				}
226: 				escaped = false
227: 			} else {
228: 				if (quoted && ch == '"') || (btQuoted && ch == '`') {
229: 					return makeToken(ch), nil
230: 				}
231: 			}
232: 			// allow quoted text to wrap continue on multiple lines
233: 			if ch == '\n' {
234: 				l.line += 1 + l.skippedLines
235: 				l.skippedLines = 0
236: 			}
237: 			// collect this character as part of the quoted token
238: 			val = append(val, ch)
239: 			continue
240: 		}
241: 
242: 		if unicode.IsSpace(ch) {
243: 			// ignore CR altogether, we only actually care about LF (\n)
244: 			if ch == '\r' {
245: 				continue
246: 			}
247: 			// end of the line
248: 			if ch == '\n' {
249: 				// newlines can be escaped to chain arguments
250: 				// onto multiple lines; else, increment the line count
251: 				if escaped {
252: 					l.skippedLines++
253: 					escaped = false
254: 				} else {
255: 					l.line += 1 + l.skippedLines
256: 					l.skippedLines = 0
257: 				}
258: 				// comments (#) are single-line only
259: 				comment = false
260: 			}
261: 			// any kind of space means we're at the end of this token
262: 			if len(val) > 0 {
263: 				return makeToken(0), nil
264: 			}
265: 			continue
266: 		}
267: 
268: 		// comments must be at the start of a token,
269: 		// in other words, preceded by space or newline
270: 		if ch == '#' && len(val) == 0 {
271: 			comment = true
272: 		}
273: 		if comment {
274: 			continue
275: 		}
276: 
277: 		if len(val) == 0 {
278: 			l.token = Token{Line: l.line}
279: 			if ch == '"' {
280: 				quoted = true
281: 				continue
282: 			}
283: 			if ch == '`' {
284: 				btQuoted = true
285: 				continue
286: 			}
287: 		}
288: 
289: 		if escaped {
290: 			// allow escaping the first < to skip the heredoc syntax
291: 			if ch == '<' {
292: 				heredocEscaped = true
293: 			} else {
294: 				val = append(val, '\\')
295: 			}
296: 			escaped = false
297: 		}
298: 
299: 		val = append(val, ch)
300: 	}
301: }

303: // finalizeHeredoc takes the runes read as the heredoc text and the marker,
304: // and processes the text to strip leading whitespace, returning the final
305: // value without the leading whitespace.
306: func (l *lexer) finalizeHeredoc(val []rune, marker string) ([]rune, error) {
307: 	stringVal := string(val)
308: 	lastNewline := l.heredocContentEnd(stringVal)
309: 	lines := l.heredocLines(stringVal, lastNewline)
310: 	paddingToStrip := l.heredocPadding(stringVal, lastNewline, marker)
311: 	out, err := l.joinHeredocLines(lines, paddingToStrip, marker, l.line)
312: 	if err != nil {
313: 		return nil, err
314: 	}
315: 	return []rune(out), nil
316: }

322: // NumLineBreaks counts how many line breaks are in the token text.
323: func (t Token) NumLineBreaks() int {
324: 	lineBreaks := strings.Count(t.Text, "\n")
325: 	if t.wasQuoted == '<' {
326: 		// heredocs have an extra linebreak because the opening
327: 		// delimiter is on its own line and is not included in the
328: 		// token Text itself, and the trailing newline is removed.
329: 		lineBreaks += 2

336: // isNextOnNewLine tests whether t2 is on a different line from t1
337: func isNextOnNewLine(t1, t2 Token) bool {
338: 	// If the second token is from a different file,
339: 	// we can assume it's from a different line
340: 	if t1.File != t2.File {
341: 		return true
342: 	}
343: 
344: 	// If the second token is from a different import chain,
345: 	// we can assume it's from a different line
346: 	if len(t1.imports) != len(t2.imports) {
347: 		return true
348: 	}
349: 	for i, im := range t1.imports {
350: 		if im != t2.imports[i] {
351: 			return true
352: 		}
353: 	}
354: 
355: 	// If the first token (incl line breaks) ends
356: 	// on a line earlier than the next token,
357: 	// then the second token is on a new line
358: 	return t1.Line+t1.NumLineBreaks() < t2.Line
359: }

361: func (l *lexer) advanceCursor() bool {
362: 	if l.cursor < len(l.tokens)-1 {
363: 		l.cursor++
364: 		return true
365: 	}

369: // Prev moves to the previous token. It does the inverse
370: // of Next(), except this function may decrement the cursor
371: // to -1 so that the next call to Next() points to the
372: // first token; this allows dispensing to "start over". This
373: // method returns true if the cursor ends up pointing to a
374: // valid token.
375: func (l *lexer) retreatCursor() bool {
376: 	if l.cursor > -1 {
377: 		l.cursor--
378: 		return l.cursor > -1
379: 	}
380: 	return false
381: }

383: // NextArg loads the next token if it is on the same
384: // line and if it is not a block opening (open curly
385: // brace). Returns true if an argument token was
386: // loaded; false otherwise. If false, all tokens on
387: // the line have been consumed except for potentially
388: // a block opening. It handles imported tokens
389: // correctly.
390: func (l *lexer) takeNextArg() bool {
391: 	if !l.cursorOnSameLine() {
392: 		return false
393: 	}
394: 	if l.currentVal() == "{" {
395: 		// roll back; a block opening is not an argument
396: 		l.cursor--
397: 		return false
398: 	}
399: 	return true
400: }

402: // nextOnSameLine advances the cursor if the next
403: // token is on the same line of the same file.
404: func (l *lexer) cursorOnSameLine() bool {
405: 	if l.cursor < 0 {
406: 		l.cursor++
407: 		return true
408: 	}
409: 	if l.cursor >= len(l.tokens)-1 {
410: 		return false
411: 	}
412: 	curr := l.tokens[l.cursor]
413: 	next := l.tokens[l.cursor+1]
414: 	if !isNextOnNewLine(curr, next) {
415: 		l.cursor++
416: 		return true
417: 	}
418: 	return false
419: }

421: // NextLine loads the next token only if it is not on the same
422: // line as the current token, and returns true if a token was
423: // loaded; false otherwise. If false, there is not another token
424: // or it is on the same line. It handles imported tokens correctly.
425: func (l *lexer) takeNextLine() bool {
426: 	if l.cursor < 0 {
427: 		l.cursor++
428: 		return true
429: 	}
430: 	if l.cursor >= len(l.tokens)-1 {
431: 		return false
432: 	}
433: 	curr := l.tokens[l.cursor]
434: 	next := l.tokens[l.cursor+1]
435: 	if isNextOnNewLine(curr, next) {
436: 		l.cursor++
437: 		return true
438: 	}
439: 	return false

442: // NextBlock can be used as the condition of a for loop
443: // to load the next token as long as it opens a block or
444: // is already in a block nested more than initialNestingLevel.
445: // In other words, a loop over NextBlock() will iterate
446: // all tokens in the block assuming the next token is an
447: // open curly brace, until the matching closing brace.
448: // The open and closing brace tokens for the outer-most
449: // block will be consumed internally and omitted from
450: // the iteration.
451: //
452: // Proper use of this method looks like this:
453: //
454: //	for nesting := l.currentNesting(); l.takeNextBlock(nesting); {
455: //	}
456: //
457: // However, in simple cases where it is known that the
458: // Dispenser is new and has not already traversed state
459: // by a loop over NextBlock(), this will do:
460: //
461: //	for l.takeNextBlock(0) {
462: //	}
463: //
464: // As with other token parsing logic, a loop over
465: // NextBlock() should be contained within a loop over
466: // Next(), as it is usually prudent to skip the initial
467: // token.
468: func (l *lexer) takeNextBlock(initialNestingLevel int) bool {
469: 	if l.nesting > initialNestingLevel {
470: 		if !l.advanceCursor() {
471: 			return false // should be EOF error
472: 		}
473: 		if l.currentVal() == "}" && !l.cursorOnSameLine() {
474: 			l.nesting--
475: 		} else if l.currentVal() == "{" && !l.cursorOnSameLine() {
476: 			l.nesting++
477: 		}
478: 		return l.nesting > initialNestingLevel
479: 	}
480: 	if !l.cursorOnSameLine() { // block must open on same line
481: 		return false
482: 	}
483: 	if l.currentVal() != "{" {
484: 		l.cursor-- // roll back if not opening brace
485: 		return false
486: 	}
487: 	l.advanceCursor() // consume open curly brace
488: 	if l.currentVal() == "}" {
489: 		return false // open and then closed right away
490: 	}
491: 	l.nesting++
492: 	return true
493: }

501: // Val gets the text of the current token. If there is no token
502: // loaded, it returns empty string.
503: func (l *lexer) currentVal() string {
504: 	if l.cursor < 0 || l.cursor >= len(l.tokens) {
505: 		return ""
506: 	}
507: 	return l.tokens[l.cursor].Text
508: }

510: // ValRaw gets the raw text of the current token (including quotes).
511: // If the token was a heredoc, then the delimiter is not included,
512: // because that is not relevant to any unmarshaling logic at this time.
513: // If there is no token loaded, it returns empty string.
514: func (l *lexer) currentValRaw() string {
515: 	if l.cursor < 0 || l.cursor >= len(l.tokens) {
516: 		return ""
517: 	}
518: 	quote := l.tokens[l.cursor].wasQuoted
519: 	if quote > 0 && quote != '<' {
520: 		// string literal
521: 		return string(quote) + l.tokens[l.cursor].Text + string(quote)
522: 	}
523: 	return l.tokens[l.cursor].Text
524: }

531: 	}

533: 	text := l.tokens[l.cursor].Text

535: 	if quote > 0 {
536: 		return text // string literal
537: 	}
538: 	if num, err := strconv.Atoi(text); err == nil {

567: // Args is a convenience function that loads the next arguments
568: // (tokens on the same line) into an arbitrary number of strings
569: // pointed to in targets. If there are not enough argument tokens
570: // available to fill targets, false is returned and the remaining
571: // targets are left unchanged. If all the targets are filled,
572: // then true is returned.
573: func (l *lexer) fillArgs(targets ...*string) bool {
574: 	for i := 0; i < len(targets); i++ {
575: 		if !l.takeNextArg() {
576: 			return false
577: 		}
578: 		*targets[i] = l.currentVal()
579: 	}
580: 	return l.cursor >= -1
581: }

583: // AllArgs is like Args, but if there are more argument tokens
584: // available than there are targets, false is returned. The
585: // number of available argument tokens must match the number of
586: // targets exactly to return true.
587: func (l *lexer) fillAllArgs(targets ...*string) bool {
588: 	if !l.fillArgs(targets...) {
589: 		return false
590: 	}
591: 	if l.takeNextArg() {
592: 		l.retreatCursor()
593: 		return false
594: 	}
595: 	return l.cursor < len(l.tokens)+1

602: 	for l.takeNextArg() {

638: // the tokens from the current token until the end of the

647: // NextSegment returns a copy of the tokens from the current
648: // token until the end of the line or block that starts at
649: // the end of the line.
650: func (l *lexer) collectNextSegment() Segment {
651: 	tkns := Segment{l.currentToken()}
652: 	for l.takeNextArg() {
653: 		tkns = append(tkns, l.currentToken())
654: 	}
655: 	var openedBlock bool
656: 	for nesting := l.currentNesting(); l.takeNextBlock(nesting); {
657: 		if !openedBlock {
658: 			// because NextBlock() consumes the initial open
659: 			// curly brace, we rewind here to append it, since
660: 			// our case is special in that we want the new
661: 			// dispenser to have all the tokens including
662: 			// surrounding curly braces
663: 			l.retreatCursor()
664: 			tkns = append(tkns, l.currentToken())
665: 			l.advanceCursor()
666: 			openedBlock = true
667: 		}
668: 		tkns = append(tkns, l.currentToken())
669: 	}
670: 	if openedBlock {
671: 		// include closing brace
672: 		tkns = append(tkns, l.currentToken())
673: 
674: 		// do not consume the closing curly brace; the
675: 		// next iteration of the enclosing loop will
676: 		// call Next() and consume it
677: 	}
678: 	return append(tkns, l.tokens[:0]...)

824: func (l *lexer) beginServerBlock() error {
825: 	if len(l.parseTokens) == 0 {
826: 		return nil
827: 	}
828: 
829: 	err := l.parseAddresses()
830: 	if err != nil {
831: 		return err
832: 	}
833: 
834: 	if l.eof {
835: 		// this happens if the Caddyfile consists of only
836: 		// a line of addresses and nothing else
837: 		return nil
838: 	}

840: 	if ok, name := l.namedRouteInfo(); ok {
841: 		// named routes only have one key, the route name
842: 		l.block.Keys = []string{name}
843: 		l.block.IsNamedRoute = true
844: 
845: 		// we just need a dummy leading token to ease parsing later
846: 		nameToken := l.parseToken()
847: 		nameToken.Text = name
848: 
849: 		// get all the tokens from the block, including the braces
850: 		tokens, err := l.collectBlockTokens(true)
851: 		if err != nil {
852: 			return err
853: 		}
854: 		tokens = append([]Token{nameToken}, tokens...)
855: 		l.block.Segments = []Segment{tokens}
856: 		return nil
857: 	}
858: 
859: 	if ok, name := l.snippetInfo(); ok {
860: 		if l.definedSnippets == nil {
861: 			l.definedSnippets = map[string][]Token{}
862: 		}
863: 		if _, found := l.definedSnippets[name]; found {
864: 			return l.parseErrf("redeclaration of previously declared snippet %s", name)
865: 		}
866: 		// consume all tokens til matched close brace
867: 		tokens, err := l.collectBlockTokens(false)
868: 		if err != nil {
869: 			return err
870: 		}
871: 		// Just as we need to track which file the token comes from, we need to
872: 		// keep track of which snippet the token comes from. This is helpful
873: 		// in tracking import cycles across files/snippets by namespacing them.
874: 		// Without this, we end up with false-positives in cycle-detection.
875: 		for k, v := range tokens {
876: 			v.snippetName = name
877: 			tokens[k] = v
878: 		}
879: 		l.definedSnippets[name] = tokens
880: 		// empty block keys so we don't save this block as a real server.
881: 		l.block.Keys = nil
882: 		return nil
883: 	}
884: 
885: 	return l.parseBlockContents()
886: }

888: func (l *lexer) parseAddresses() error {
889: 	var expectingAnother bool
890: 
891: 	for {
892: 		tkn := l.parseVal()
893: 
894: 		// special case: import directive replaces tokens during parse-time
895: 		if tkn == "import" && l.parseIsNewLine() {
896: 			err := l.processImport(0)
897: 			if err != nil {
898: 				return err
899: 			}
900: 			continue
901: 		}
902: 
903: 		// Open brace definitely indicates end of addresses
904: 		if tkn == "{" {
905: 			if expectingAnother {
906: 				return l.parseErrf("Expected another address but had '%s' - check for extra comma", tkn)
907: 			}
908: 			// Mark this server block as being defined with braces.
909: 			// This is used to provide a better error message when
910: 			// the user may have tried to define two server blocks
911: 			// without having used braces, which are required in
912: 			// that case.
913: 			l.block.HasBraces = true
914: 			break
915: 		}
916: 
917: 		// Users commonly forget to place a space between the address and the '{'
918: 		if strings.HasSuffix(tkn, "{") {
919: 			return l.parseErrf("Site addresses cannot end with a curly brace: '%s' - put a space between the token and the brace", tkn)
920: 		}
921: 
922: 		if tkn != "" { // empty token possible if user typed ""
923: 			// Trailing comma indicates another address will follow, which
924: 			// may possibly be on the next line
925: 			if tkn[len(tkn)-1] == ',' {
926: 				tkn = tkn[:len(tkn)-1]
927: 				expectingAnother = true
928: 			} else {
929: 				expectingAnother = false // but we may still see another one on this line
930: 			}
931: 
932: 			// If there's a comma here, it's probably because they didn't use a space
933: 			// between their two domains, e.g. "foo.com,bar.com", which would not be
934: 			// parsed as two separate site addresses.
935: 			if strings.Contains(tkn, ",") {
936: 				return l.parseErrf("Site addresses cannot contain a comma ',': '%s' - put a space after the comma to separate site addresses", tkn)
937: 			}
938: 
939: 			l.block.Keys = append(l.block.Keys, tkn)
940: 		}
941: 
942: 		// Advance token and possibly break out of loop or return error
943: 		hasNext := l.parseAdvance()
944: 		if expectingAnother && !hasNext {
945: 			return l.parseEOFErr()
946: 		}
947: 		if !hasNext {
948: 			l.eof = true
949: 			break // EOF
950: 		}
951: 		if !expectingAnother && l.parseIsNewLine() {
952: 			break
953: 		}
954: 	}
955: 
956: 	return nil
957: }

959: func (l *lexer) parseBlockContents() error {
960: 	errOpenCurlyBrace := l.expectOpenBrace()

963: 		l.parseCursor--
964: 	}

966: 	err := l.parseDirectives()
967: 	if err != nil {
968: 		return err
969: 	}

971: 	// only look for close curly brace if there was an opening
972: 	if errOpenCurlyBrace == nil {
973: 		err = l.expectCloseBrace()
974: 		if err != nil {
975: 			return err
976: 		}
977: 	}

980: }

982: // directives parses through all the lines for directives
983: // and it expects the next token to be the first
984: // directive. It goes until EOF or closing curly brace
985: // which ends the server block.

987: 	for l.parseAdvance() {
988: 		// end of server block
989: 		if l.parseVal() == "}" {
990: 			// l.parseNesting has already been decremented
991: 			break
992: 		}

994: 		// special case: import directive replaces tokens during parse-time
995: 		if l.parseVal() == "import" {
996: 			err := l.processImport(1)
997: 			if err != nil {
998: 				return err
999: 			}
1000: 			l.parseCursor-- // cursor is advanced when we continue, so roll back one more
1001: 			continue
1002: 		}
1003: 
1004: 		// normal case: parse a directive as a new segment
1005: 		// (a "segment" is a line which starts with a directive
1006: 		// and which ends at the end of the line or at the end of
1007: 		// the block that is opened at the end of the line)
1008: 		if err := l.parseDirective(); err != nil {
1009: 			return err
1010: 		}
1011: 	}
1012: 
1013: 	return nil
1014: }

1016: // doImport swaps out the import directive and its argument
1017: // (a total of 2 tokens) with the tokens in the specified file
1018: // or globbing pattern. When the function returns, the cursor
1019: // is on the token before where the import directive was. In
1020: // other words, call Next() to access the first token that was
1021: // imported.
1022: func (l *lexer) processImport(nesting int) error {
1023: 	// syntax checks
1024: 	if !l.parseNextArg() {
1025: 		return l.parseArgErr()
1026: 	}
1027: 	importPattern := l.parseVal()
1028: 	if importPattern == "" {
1029: 		return l.parseErr("Import requires a non-empty filepath")
1030: 	}
1031: 
1032: 	// grab remaining args as placeholder replacements
1033: 	args := l.parseRemainingArgs()
1034: 
1035: 	// set up a replacer for non-variadic args replacement
1036: 	repl := makeArgsReplacer(args)
1037: 
1038: 	// splice out the import directive and its arguments
1039: 	// (2 tokens, plus the length of args)
1040: 	tokensBefore := l.parseTokens[:l.parseCursor-1-len(args)]
1041: 	tokensAfter := l.parseTokens[l.parseCursor+1:]
1042: 	var importedTokens []Token
1043: 	var nodes []string
1044: 
1045: 	// first check snippets. That is a simple, non-recursive replacement
1046: 	if l.definedSnippets != nil && l.definedSnippets[importPattern] != nil {
1047: 		importedTokens = l.definedSnippets[importPattern]
1048: 		if len(importedTokens) > 0 {
1049: 			// just grab the first one
1050: 			nodes = append(nodes, fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", importedTokens[0].File, importedTokens[0].snippetName))
1051: 		}
1052: 	} else {
1053: 		// make path relative to the file of the _token_ being processed rather
1054: 		// than current working directory (issue #867) and then use glob to get
1055: 		// list of matching filenames
1056: 		absFile, err := filepath.Abs(l.parseFile())
1057: 		if err != nil {
1058: 			return l.parseErrf("Failed to get absolute path of file: %s: %v", l.parseFile(), err)
1059: 		}
1060: 
1061: 		var matches []string
1062: 		var globPattern string
1063: 		if !filepath.IsAbs(importPattern) {
1064: 			globPattern = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(absFile), importPattern)
1065: 		} else {
1066: 			globPattern = importPattern
1067: 		}
1068: 		if strings.Count(globPattern, "*") > 1 || strings.Count(globPattern, "?") > 1 ||
1069: 			(strings.Contains(globPattern, "[") && strings.Contains(globPattern, "]")) {
1070: 			// See issue #2096 - a pattern with many glob expansions can hang for too long
1071: 			return l.parseErrf("Glob pattern may only contain one wildcard (*), but has others: %s", globPattern)
1072: 		}
1073: 		matches, err = filepath.Glob(globPattern)
1074: 
1075: 		if err != nil {
1076: 			return l.parseErrf("Failed to use import pattern %s: %v", importPattern, err)
1077: 		}
1078: 		if len(matches) == 0 {
1079: 			if strings.ContainsAny(globPattern, "*?[]") {
1080: 				caddy.Log().Warn("No files matching import glob pattern", zap.String("pattern", importPattern))
1081: 			} else {
1082: 				return l.parseErrf("File to import not found: %s", importPattern)
1083: 			}
1084: 		} else {
1085: 			// See issue #5295 - should skip any files that start with a . when iterating over them.
1086: 			sep := string(filepath.Separator)
1087: 			segGlobPattern := strings.Split(globPattern, sep)
1088: 			if strings.HasPrefix(segGlobPattern[len(segGlobPattern)-1], "*") {
1089: 				var tmpMatches []string
1090: 				for _, m := range matches {
1091: 					seg := strings.Split(m, sep)
1092: 					if !strings.HasPrefix(seg[len(seg)-1], ".") {
1093: 						tmpMatches = append(tmpMatches, m)
1094: 					}
1095: 				}
1096: 				matches = tmpMatches
1097: 			}
1098: 		}
1099: 
1100: 		// collect all the imported tokens
1101: 		for _, importFile := range matches {
1102: 			newTokens, err := l.processSingleImport(importFile)
1103: 			if err != nil {
1104: 				return err
1105: 			}
1106: 			importedTokens = append(importedTokens, newTokens...)
1107: 		}
1108: 		nodes = matches
1109: 	}
1110: 
1111: 	nodeName := l.parseFile()
1112: 	if l.parseToken().snippetName != "" {
1113: 		nodeName += fmt.Sprintf(":%s", l.parseToken().snippetName)
1114: 	}
1115: 	tmpGraph := &lexer{importNodes: l.parseImportNodes, importEdges: l.parseImportEdges}
1116: 	tmpGraph.addImportNode(nodeName)
1117: 	l.parseImportNodes = tmpGraph.importNodes
1118: 	l.parseImportEdges = tmpGraph.importEdges
1119: 	tmpGraph.addImportNodes(nodes)
1120: 	l.parseImportNodes = tmpGraph.importNodes
1121: 	l.parseImportEdges = tmpGraph.importEdges
1122: 	if err := tmpGraph.addImportEdges(nodeName, nodes); err != nil {
1123: 		tmpGraph.removeImportNodes(nodes)
1124: 		l.parseImportNodes = tmpGraph.importNodes
1125: 		l.parseImportEdges = tmpGraph.importEdges
1126: 		return err
1127: 	}
1128: 	l.parseImportNodes = tmpGraph.importNodes
1129: 	l.parseImportEdges = tmpGraph.importEdges
1130: 
1131: 	// copy the tokens so we don't overwrite l.definedSnippets
1132: 	tokensCopy := make([]Token, 0, len(importedTokens))
1133: 
1134: 	var (
1135: 		maybeSnippet   bool
1136: 		maybeSnippetId bool
1137: 		index          int
1138: 	)
1139: 
1140: 	// run the argument replacer on the tokens
1141: 	// golang for range slice return a copy of value
1142: 	// similarly, append also copy value
1143: 	for i, token := range importedTokens {
1144: 		// update the token's imports to refer to import directive filename, line number and snippet name if there is one
1145: 		if token.snippetName != "" {
1146: 			token.imports = append(token.imports, fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d (import %s)", l.parseFile(), l.parseLine(), token.snippetName))
1147: 		} else {
1148: 			token.imports = append(token.imports, fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d (import)", l.parseFile(), l.parseLine()))
1149: 		}
1150: 
1151: 		// naive way of determine snippets, as snippets definition can only follow name + block
1152: 		// format, won't check for nesting correctness or any other error, that's what parser does.
1153: 		if !maybeSnippet && nesting == 0 {
1154: 			// first of the line
1155: 			if i == 0 || isNextOnNewLine(tokensCopy[i-1], token) {
1156: 				index = 0
1157: 			} else {
1158: 				index++
1159: 			}
1160: 
1161: 			if index == 0 && len(token.Text) >= 3 && strings.HasPrefix(token.Text, "(") && strings.HasSuffix(token.Text, ")") {
1162: 				maybeSnippetId = true
1163: 			}
1164: 		}
1165: 
1166: 		switch token.Text {
1167: 		case "{":
1168: 			nesting++
1169: 			if index == 1 && maybeSnippetId && nesting == 1 {
1170: 				maybeSnippet = true
1171: 				maybeSnippetId = false
1172: 			}
1173: 		case "}":
1174: 			nesting--
1175: 			if nesting == 0 && maybeSnippet {
1176: 				maybeSnippet = false
1177: 			}
1178: 		}
1179: 
1180: 		if maybeSnippet {
1181: 			tokensCopy = append(tokensCopy, token)
1182: 			continue
1183: 		}
1184: 
1185: 		foundVariadic, startIndex, endIndex := parseVariadic(token, len(args))
1186: 		if foundVariadic {
1187: 			for _, arg := range args[startIndex:endIndex] {
1188: 				token.Text = arg
1189: 				tokensCopy = append(tokensCopy, token)
1190: 			}
1191: 		} else {
1192: 			token.Text = repl.ReplaceKnown(token.Text, "")
1193: 			tokensCopy = append(tokensCopy, token)
1194: 		}
1195: 	}
1196: 
1197: 	// splice the imported tokens in the place of the import statement
1198: 	// and rewind cursor so Next() will land on first imported token
1199: 	l.parseTokens = append(tokensBefore, append(tokensCopy, tokensAfter...)...)
1200: 	l.parseCursor -= len(args) + 1
1201: 
1202: 	return nil
1203: }

1205: // doSingleImport lexes the individual file at importFile and returns
1206: // its tokens or an error, if any.
1207: func (l *lexer) processSingleImport(importFile string) ([]Token, error) {
1208: 	l.parseCursor += len(l.parseTokens[:0])

1213: 	defer file.Close()
1214:

1216: 		return nil, l.parseErrf("Could not import %s: %v", importFile, err)
1217: 	} else if info.IsDir() {
1218: 		return nil, l.parseErrf("Could not import %s: is a directory", importFile)

1220:

1222: 	if err != nil {
1223: 		return nil, l.parseErrf("Could not read imported file %s: %v", importFile, err)
1224: 	}
1225:

1233: 	if err != nil {
1234: 		return nil, l.parseErrf("Could not read tokens while importing %s: %v", importFile, err)

1250: // directive collects tokens until the directive's scope
1251: // closes (either end of line or end of curly brace block).
1252: // It expects the currently-loaded token to be a directive
1253: // (or } that ends a server block). The collected tokens
1254: // are loaded into the current server block for later use
1255: // by directive setup functions.
1256: func (l *lexer) parseDirective() error {
1257: 	// a segment is a list of tokens associated with this directive
1258: 	var segment Segment
1259: 
1260: 	// the directive itself is appended as a relevant token
1261: 	segment = append(segment, l.parseToken())
1262: 
1263: 	for l.parseAdvance() {
1264: 		if l.parseVal() == "{" {
1265: 			l.parseNesting++
1266: 			if !l.parseIsNextOnNewLine() && l.parseToken().wasQuoted == 0 {
1267: 				return l.parseErr("Unexpected next token after '{' on same line")
1268: 			}
1269: 			if l.parseIsNewLine() {
1270: 				return l.parseErr("Unexpected '{' on a new line; did you mean to place the '{' on the previous line?")
1271: 			}
1272: 		} else if l.parseVal() == "{}" {
1273: 			if l.parseIsNextOnNewLine() && l.parseToken().wasQuoted == 0 {
1274: 				return l.parseErr("Unexpected '{}' at end of line")
1275: 			}
1276: 		} else if l.parseIsNewLine() && l.parseNesting == 0 {
1277: 			l.parseCursor-- // read too far
1278: 			break
1279: 		} else if l.parseVal() == "}" && l.parseNesting > 0 {
1280: 			l.parseNesting--
1281: 		} else if l.parseVal() == "}" && l.parseNesting == 0 {
1282: 			return l.parseErr("Unexpected '}' because no matching opening brace")
1283: 		} else if l.parseVal() == "import" && l.parseIsNewLine() {
1284: 			if err := l.processImport(1); err != nil {
1285: 				return err
1286: 			}
1287: 			l.parseCursor-- // cursor is advanced when we continue, so roll back one more
1288: 			continue
1289: 		}
1290: 
1291: 		segment = append(segment, l.parseToken())
1292: 	}
1293: 
1294: 	l.block.Segments = append(l.block.Segments, segment)
1295: 
1296: 	if l.parseNesting > 0 {
1297: 		return l.parseEOFErr()
1298: 	}
1299: 
1300: 	return nil
1301: }

1346: func (l *lexer) collectBlockTokens(retainCurlies bool) ([]Token, error) {
1347: 	// block must have curlies.
1348: 	err := l.expectOpenBrace()

1350: 		return nil, err
1351: 	}
1352: 	nesting := 1 // count our own nesting
1353: 	tokens := []Token{}
1354: 	if retainCurlies {
1355: 		tokens = append(tokens, l.parseToken())

1357: 	for l.parseAdvance() {
1358: 		if l.parseVal() == "}" {
1359: 			nesting--
1360: 			if nesting == 0 {
1361: 				if retainCurlies {
1362: 					tokens = append(tokens, l.parseToken())

1368: 			nesting++
1369: 		}
1370: 		tokens = append(tokens, l.parseTokens[l.parseCursor])
1371: 	}

1373: 	if nesting != 0 {
1374: 		return nil, l.parseSyntaxErr("}")
1375: 	}

1614: 			}

1620: 		if l.fmtHandleBackslash(ch) {
1621: 			continue

1624: 			continue
1625: 		}
1626: 		if l.fmtHandleQuoted(ch) {
1627: 			continue

part.text:
Fixed. The issue was in the Caddyfile lexer (caddyconfig/caddyfile/lexer.go): any token starting with `<<` was unconditionally treated as a heredoc opening, so `between << >>` made the lexer collect `  >>` as a "heredoc marker" and fail.

The change mirrors the upstream fix:
- A space after `<<...` now ends the token normally (so `<<` and `>>` lex as plain tokens), instead of continuing to scan for a marker
- The `<<<` / marker validation only happens when the token runs to the end of the line (newline), with a new "missing opening heredoc marker" error for a bare `<<`
- Heredoc detection is now also skipped inside quoted/backtick strings

Verified: all `caddyconfig/caddyfile` tests pass (including the previously failing heredoc lexer cases), and a throwaway end-to-end check confirmed `between << >>` now tokenizes correctly while real heredocs still work.
